reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is another stunning beach on the  southern coast of Portugal and a bit of a walk from our hotel, RIU Club Hotel Guarana. Getting to this beach included  the descent of 120 plus steps, going down counted 125 on the way back up 126 (rough idea).We visited this beautiful place a number of times during our 2 week holiday.Just at the bottom of the steps is Praia do Barranco das Belhalruchus which eventually leads  to this amazing beach with its dramatic multicoloured sandstone cliffs.From Praia das Belhalruchus there is a temporary boardwalk along the back of the beach, it runs out by the Sheraton Hotel sun beds (blue towels). That is where Praia Falesia beginsThere are no sunbeds or umbrellas here, in fact there are no facilities on this beach, there are 2 restaurants on Praia das Belhalruchus, Mare and O Golphino.Ideal spot to spread out the beach mats and towels, relax enjoy the glorious sunshine and the stunning scenery.Would recommend visiting this beach, it is much less crowded than the beach next door. Would also recommend to bring some water, or something to drink.From Praia das Belhalruchus through Praia Falesia, is a very popular walk, which eventually leads to Vilamoura, it is a lengthy walk.It is important to maintain this beautiful area that visitors take all their rubbish home with them or make use of the bins provided.Every now and again beach sellers turn up, selling table cloths etc, or drinks, they are no hassle, just say no thanks and they go away.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great time
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely area to relax and chill out in the sun. Unlike a lot of beach's you are left alone. Near to shops and restaurants, without hearing them

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely walk from Vilamoura to Olhos do Agua
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful sandy beach shielded from inland by the cliffs. At Vilamoura end there are several beach restaurants and facilities on the first half mile from the marina. If you are feeling fit then it is about an hour and a half walk to the pretty resort of Olhos De Agua which is accessed either by a steep set of wooden steps or an adventurous climb over the "dunes" onto the very small beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach for lovely walks
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went for a walk along the beech every day for an hour or so. Clean and lovely views of Falesia beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had a great day at this beach but was really windy and there was big waves, although my daughter had a great time they were quite strong. Steps down to beach so bear on mind if you have elderly or buggies/wheelchairs etc. Beach bar at top good with reasonable priced coffee, sandwiches etc.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: falesia beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A really stunning beach lots of vistors but superb sand and great views , water is cold with biggish waves , few places around europe are better than here .A place to spend the day for sunworshipers

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We just returned from a fantastic week at hotel Tui Blue Falesia above the beach . We walked to Villamoura 7km it was absolutely amazing and the sea was warm . It really is a wonderful beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: amazing beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: amazing view and water. Even in Oktober the water was still amazing. I can Imagine in july and august would be overcrowded. In October was amazing. Remembered on Canoa Quebrada / Brasil

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cracking and clean beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: As per title. Clean beach with stunning coloured cliffs as backdrop. Selection of beach bars to choose from.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Outstanding
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There is no comparison between this beach and the one at Olhos d'Agua.  The latter is a small bay but this one runs for over 6 km, almost to Vilamoura.  The only problem is that there are 125 steps down to the beach and the same number when you want to return.When we were there the sea was rather rough and people were trying to surf the waves. Behind the beach are some very colourful cliffs and there were hang gliders flying from them further down the beach.There are two beach cafes but because of where they are they are expensive €4 for a can of coke and €10 for a bottle of beer.  Well worth a visit if you are in the area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Long beach with impressive cliff
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wow! This was my first word when I saw it from the top of the stairs. The place is stunning, kilometers of sandy beaches next to this 50 meters wall of coloured sandstone.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely long sandy beach and great for a day out. The beach is a bit of a mission to get to if you’ve a pushchair we had to carry it down and up the steps. There’s a cafe/bar at the top which is very good. One tip is don’t use the sun beds on the right as there very expensive and the sun bed man stinks like a polecat on heat and can be rude when you question his prices ( €5 extra than other beaches we’ve visited locally) but having the little one with us we needed shade but we had a lovely peaceful day doing all the normal beach stuff, swimming, reading etc

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wide and long....
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Praia Falesia is one of longest Algarve sandy beaches. It could be reached by car, but mostly through the few hotels in the first row to the ocean, like Pine Cliffs (Sheraton), Portobay Felasia...There are sunbeds and sunshades available for a 15 Eur/day. There are also a few bars where you could have a drink or a light meal.A good choice to enjoy the ocean.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular Red Cliff Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Red beautiful beach red cliffs blue ocean umbrella pine trees!!! Horse back riding massages great packed sand for running!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Can't be beaten
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful long stretch of beach - a bit steep getting down - but worth the visit - stunning cliffs and views

reviewsWithKeywords.title: clean pleasant beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: nice sandy beach. Sunbeads available. Lifeguard presence. Bit of  a climb up and down if you have buggy/disabled person not great accessiblity. Bar nearby at top of steps.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach and lovely restaurants to eat at.people really nice and the views are amazing would definitely go back.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: amazing beach with orange coloured cliffs
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you like walking a beach this is the one for you.  7km of golden sand, with relentless waves and a beautiful back drop of orange cliffs.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful !
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited everyday! Beautiful, not crowded, and lovely to swim in. Well worth a visit. The sea can be quite strong and I can see why lifeguards are there. Loved just lying on a beach towel all day relaxing. A bar/snacks is available just before walking down the steps to the beach. Has clean toilets also.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing Beach !!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach has to be one of the most amazing beaches in the Algarve , You can walk along to Olhos D Agua along the beach at low tide . 2 beach restaurants , and you can find a quiet spot , Love it

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very clean beach, with lifeguard. Sun loungers were €5 each, also a snack bar for drinks etc. Absolutely worth a visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with amazing colours. The only down side is the sand. Sand is a bit rough and if you're not careful you can hurt your feet.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Only had a look .
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We are not beach lovers do we just had a quick look...it's absolutely stunning.. gets a few photos..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It is rated : one of the most beautiful beaches in the world
reviewsWithKeywords.text: And this title is well deserved:You have to see it at least 3 times: sunrise; sunset; during the day.If you are lucky (like us) and you see it in winter, you are alone in the beach, big storm, high waves, water of silver colour, you know how perfection looks like.Of course winter means temperatures around 15 to 18 degrees; so you don’t freeze. But resist the temptation to go swimming: there is always a wave that surprises you and you get wet feet while shooting photos and videosBut in the sea, you are « gone with the wind »

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth all the steps!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were staying at nearby hotel. The steps down are in good condition and easy to negotiate. The beach is amazing! Truly an unforgettable experience. The cliffs are so picturesque and the sea is litter free and clean. We enjoyed several walks along here and would thoroughly recommend.However climbing the steps back up was taxing but with rest along the way we survived!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fabulous 5 mile beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful 5 mile long beach, the best on the Algarve. Ask locally for the directions from the town (approx. 15 minute walk).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice clean beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely clean beach with fresh wind blowing in from the Atlantic,water is cold but beautifully clear,I'm sure if give it a visit you'll enjoy it

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely Walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Walked this beach from Ohos d’Agua to Vilamoura which took around 2 hours. Lovely and clean with plenty of stops available en route.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is beautiful and goes on for miles. Very clean and plenty of space for all. The sea was clear but very wavy which we liked.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful beach at the base of the stairs from the 3HB resort. The beach is clean, there are loungers to rent but also plenty of sand to pitch your own umbrella. There are washrooms at the restaurants. The water is clean and was warm and wavy in September. It was also a quieter and less crowded beach than others we went to.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach with lovely rocks
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Was staying at the Falesia Hotel and went out a couple of times at 07:30,  Turn right out of the doors, down the steps and right at the bottom.  Then hug the road around to the right, turning right at every junction (signposted to the beach).  Steep slope and steps down to the beach and then turn right and beautiful walk with hardly anyone on the beach at that time in the morning and the sun just coming up.  So peaceful and quiet.  Walk all the way along until you get to the café.  Walk up the wooden man-made path (with steps) and take the lift up to Pine Cliffs resort.  Bear slightly left at the top, across the grass and go in through the doors at the back of the Sheraton Hotel.  Walk through and come out the front, follow the road around to the exit and then bear right and it takes you back to the Falesia Hotel.  With a reasonably brisk pace it takes an hour.  There are steps so bear this in mind.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The beach with rocky orange cliffs!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We enjoyed a day at the beach. The access to the beach was good (through the resort). Not my favourite type of sand, a bit chunky for me, I prefer thin sand. The surroundings are very nice with the orange rocky cliffs. Not my favourite beach in Portugal but it is ok.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Long, beautiful beach. Clean and flat. Beach bar available and water sports. Great for swimming, clear water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: water full of weeds,
reviewsWithKeywords.text: no restaurants or cafe around, very disappointed. It is supposed to be one of the best beaches in Europe. Hello

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just perfect !!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely beautiful beach with great facilities. The Golfinho Restaurant  is conveniently located offering a great range of drinks and food and shower/wc. A friendly welcome every day !! Would definitely recommend.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very clean beach. Restaurants are 5 minutes walking distance to enjoy the whole day there. Parking is sometimes a bit difficult

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach was beautiful. Alot of sun beds and shades if you wanted but we walked a little way from them and had a lovely quiet spot under the cliffs.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Really good!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach not so many people in September. Good view with the rocks. There are options for nice lunch.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach and views but not if you have mobility issues
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A number of hotels offer courtesy buses to the beach we chose to walk, not that far from most of the hotels. When you arrive the views are beautiful but you are faced with hundreds of steps down and then later back up. Steps in excellent condition with handrail but if you have any mobility concerns you would be best to travel to another beach. Lots of beds available, or just sit on the sand from which you can walk gently into the sea to cool off.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely but very busy!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach looks really lovely as you approach it from above. There are roughly seventy steps to climb down before reaching it though - you have to climb back up at the end of the day remember! Once on the beach you can hire sun beds and umbrellas or shades or you can take your own. If you take your own then there are certain areas where you are not allowed to put your umbrella i.e. in front of the hired equipment which is a good idea. Unfortunately for us the beach was a little too crowded which is only to be expected in school holidays and the height of the season. I would like to visit the beach again though but maybe late June or early September before the crowds arrive.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went in August 2018, beautiful hotel, the Tui reps were lovely and every member of staff were friendly and helpful. Everyone works really hard to make your stay superb. Food is plentiful and the quality is great. Overall 10/10 thank you for the best holiday we will be visiting again.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach, Great Views!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a lovely beach! To access the beach you walk down hundreds of wooden steps, this is an adventure in itself! Te beach is amazing to walk on. Very scenic and picturesque!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: day by the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: love this popular beach, hired a beach lounger for 6 euroes each for the day..we were with elderly parents so only choice..very clean beach and toilets and cafe at top of several steps..not suitable for wheel chairs difficulty with walking down or up stairs..lovely day..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth the hike down the steps!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is truly breathtaking.  It’s about 7km of glorious sandy beach with beds for hire along the way.  The cliffs are red and white rock a bit similar to the isle of white with better weather & really warm sea.   The cliffs are known for providing great wind cover.  We came here 3 times.  Our first visit was nearest to Olhos de Água  but be mindful there are a lot of steps to get to the beach. We strolled along about 3/4 miles to The main falasia beach and got an Uber back only €5.50 as we didn’t really know where we were we & walked through a big hotel complex & got in the cab near the bleu hotel.  On our next visits we had a hire car & drove to the main area of Falasia beach - there are still a number of steps but not so arduous.  The weather is fantastic about 27oC ideal for walking & lazing.  There are plenty of water sports along the beach if you are interested & surf learning & hire shops.  The beach vendors are Portuguese selling local stuff mainly ground towels and dresses - be sure to haggle their prices down. They are friendly and will instantly go away if you say you are not interested no hassle for sure! This is a true treasure totally unspoilt a must see put it on your must do list if you are in the region I can not recommend it enough - truly beautiful!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth the walk..
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Many ways to get it on foot.. Great view from the cliff top.. We used the route through the Rui Hotel complex.. Good steps down.. Wide sandy beach.. Bars every so often if you fancy a walk to Vilamoura.. We did.. And got a cab bag..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Perfect beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Rolling cliffs, temped waters and lots of space. Perfect beach to spend the day with family, partner or friends

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Away from the pool
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach has access from our hotel the Portobay via wooden stairs so it is worth a visit. This year the beach was very busy unlike last year so it has become very popular.There are sunbed available to hire but these need attention as they have seen better days. Chairs are very close together so not much room to turn chairs when the sun moves around.There is a lovely beach restaurant serving fresh fish which is not to be missed.Both worth a visit, but remember the stairs back to the hotel after a relaxing day in the sun.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: You got to go there !!!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Incredible beach, very high cliffs.Water was a little cold but very refreshing. The city should consider providing bathroom facilities.  This is a must see if you are in the Faro / Albufeira area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best Beach Ever!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Excellent views, clean, fantastic for famalies, use entrance at Olhas Da Agua for most scenic view, good parking here also.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful wide sweep of sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful spot with gently sloping golden sand. You need to find the access points to the beach - generally near hotels. Some have steep steps such as near Epic Sana. Others where there is a car park have a long slow climb eg Olhos de Agua or in Vilamoura no slope at all. From Vilamoura to Olhos de Agua you can walk about 5 miles before you have to cut inland. Low red and yellow unstable cliffs fringe the beach. The sand is very wide at low tide and all along is excellent for making sand castles and structures. Life guards and pay to lay sun beds and shades and a few cafes every half mile or so where the access points are.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great Beach with lots of shells to hunt around for, water is great fun but can get choppy with is still fun but not so good for the kids if they are nervous.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very clean
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I think this is one of the best beaches in Europe. It is very clean with an interesting cliff backdrop to it. There are plenty of sun loungers for hire and a few beach cafe/bars too. Very pleasant to walk on.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Tranquil
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My husband and I visited this beach a few times whilst we were on our weeks holiday, it was so beautiful, peaceful and clean, the rock formation and views were amazing. We found the steps down to beach ok as we went down the 300 odd steps and came up the 100 step way, which you will find up the side of the cafe where the Portuguese flag flys and through the Carpark on the left. Can not wait to visit this beach again

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with usually warm water and soft sand. Always very clean, great for swimming, sunbathing and long walks by the sea. Has lots of places to eat and drink all along the beach. A must visit beach of the Algarve

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach but with very strong waves! Only 9 euros a day to hire a lounger, great value for money. There was a snack bar at the top of the stairs which was really handy. Would visit again!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach , very clean , sun beds available and not expensive No litter or cigarette dimps as you may find on other beaches

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Romantic stroll
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Staying at the resort nearby lots of steps to get down, but it was safe.Quiet, locally used beachBeach bars along the beach - nice for snacks or dinnerFriendly staffClean sandy beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely beach with some water sports activities to do. Can always find a quiet spot if you are what it

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful quiet sandy beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A steep climb, was worth it to visit this lovely beach, the ocre  coloured cliffs,topped with pine trees,  yellow sand and clean ocean.   However, difficult for anyone with mobility issues, but that does mean the beach is relatively quiet for a resort beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach with water sports
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited with my husband , 9 and 10 year old whilst staying in the Algarve as 15mins drive from Loule where we were staying. Parking free and plenty of space on the hill leading down to the beach or at the top in the road. Bar/cafe at the top of steps leading down to the beach which has the usual sun bed and parisole areas. Lots of water sports on offer, my son and husband tried paddle boarding for 15 Euro’s. One of the best beaches in the Vilamoura area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: You would be hard pushed not to find a beautiful beach in this area but Falésia Beach is something special. A short 15 minute walk from our hotel, the beach is down a fairly steep hill and then accessed by wooden steps but definitely worth the effort. Stunning views, especially at sunset, the area is picture prefect and clean, great for families with plenty of space for you lounger or towel.Well worth a visit!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is pure paradise long beach amazing cliffs and it is clean. You can have great walks here and also enjoy the lovely sunset.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gorgeous beach that goes on for quite a way so definitely one for a long walk if you fancy it. At the top where the stairs are it is very busy but if you wander down for 10 minutes or so there are quieter sections of the beach. Bit of a walk down but 100% worth it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stayed up the hill at falesia gardens stunning beach  very clean and well kept  not as busy as other beaches near by

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: No words can do this beach justice as it’s absolutely beautiful. Gets really busy but you can really appreciate it’s beauty early hours when the sun is coming up in peace and quiet around 6am was my favourite time. Starts getting busy about 9 /9:30Runs for a fair few miles all the way to vilamoura and has a number of cafes water sports etc along the way. Good day out for all. Plenty of loungers and umbrellas if needed at certain parts of the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Long sandy beach with quiet areas
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The orange cliffs make this beach stand out from the rest.- lovely for a long stroll in the shallows. You can go for miles!Several areas protected by life guards - but note these get very crowded with tourists and locals alike. Nevertheless, just a few metres walk and you can find a peaceful stretch. Sea can be rough with strong currents, but usually lovely.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Clean beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved having a swim in the sea. There were clear boundaries that people had made. If you walked to the right, children occupied that beach with games and floats and loudness and on the left, adults only and quiet. There is a shower there to wash yourself afterwards and even an option to have a massage out in the open. We had great weather in August and would highly recommend this beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Falesia Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful clean beach   a steep climb down from the main street but well worth the climb  not to over run

reviewsWithKeywords.title: exelent beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach to go to. Exelent restaurant. Parking is almost unavailable. The water temp is ideal for all.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Absolutely Gorgeous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited the beach in the morning and at night. The backdrop is unique and worth the trip alone. We walked the beach for awhile and the scenery is gorgeous.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful backdrop
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Worth a visit. It was very crowded but that seems to be the Algarve in July-August. Arrive early to get parking.  This is a long beach compared to most beaches in this area. The cliffs are a beautiful red and white. Very nice.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice but crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The sand was fine, the rock was beautiful, the waves were great, the view is nice but it is so so crowded...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is large and goes for miles which in turn means you can find space.The sand has a lot of small shells in it however you can find areas where it is pure sand.The sea seems to have a little bit of seaweed floating in it but it's not enough to put you off. I would prefer to come here over the beach right next to us in the old town Albufeira as it is extremely busy there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great vibe
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a lovely beach. We got here at 10.15, would recommend getting here an hour earlier. There are sun beds here. It is a walk down from the car park to the steps, which then take you down to the beach (79 in total, we counted), we managed fine with a 3 year old. It does get very busy, but it has a great vibe. If you want more space, walk further down and the crowd thins out. It is quite unique to go to beach with red cliffs behind.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Can walk for miles, sea is different every day due to the tides. Some watersports, jet ski, paddle boards, pedalos, flying sofa. Could do with a little beach shop selling refreshments there are a couple of restaurants.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach in Algarve
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not even too crowded, for a EUROPEAN beach. Gentle 1 foot rollers at low tide. Beach goes on forever!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Falesia beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely and clean life guards there all day really nice beach plenty of places to buy food there if need be

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Had to do the walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: They said it was a challenge due to the number of steps down to the beach in 35c they were right but well worth the sweat and toil nice clean beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach, great walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Outstanding clean beach backed by spectacular red cliffs that are a photographers dream.  My recommendation walk the length of the beach from Falesia to Vilamoura (about 3.5miles, have a nice drink on arrival, take in the sights and walk back over the cliffs, brilliant. Of course you can always catch a bus back they run at regular intervals so give it a go and enjoy the whole occasion.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Unique and very nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: An excellent, clean, beautiful beach set in a unique landscape. Apart from the absence of a beach bar, it offers all the other facilities (surveillance, water sports, hats, etc). The visitors / vacationers must however have in mind some aspects that may not please: access to the beach is done through a staircase with 80 steps; July and August have quite a few people (peak of the Algarve / Summer / vacation) so the space in the sand may not abound; the beach itself does not have a support bar; there is yes but on-site access to the beach. Of regret that some occupants deface the cliff with some trash (bags, bottles, papers) and go up the finds to write in the same. The cliff wants itself as it is: natural. For the wear already enough is promoted by nature.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Probably one of the most beautiful beaches in Europe
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Saw many beaches and for example the ones in Sardegna are on a high level but Falesia with the colorful rocks is extraordinary.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved the beach. Water sports available too. Clean and sunbed hire available.  White sands, orange cliffs and blue sea.  Beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice clean beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I would recommend Falésia beach , very clean and so vast , it is very popular but if you don’t mind walking from the steps in either direction along the beach you can always find a spot with room , toilets are in the bars situated along the beach and snacks are available there too, the sea was cold on one particular day we went , with a drift from the Atlantic coming in but that’s nature ! We were staying near Olhos d’Agua and walked from Falésia to there along the shore when the tide was out , fantastic end to the day

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beech is beautiful, golden sand and lovely clear water. Two restaurant/bars on the beech. Pedlows available and other waste r sports. Mixture of tourists and local people visiting the beech which creates a lovely atmosphere.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Miles and miles of soft sandy beach...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a very long beach.  It's a fair few steps down to it, with the only bar being at the top of the steps.  There are no toilets close by.  The sea is safe, you can hire beds and parasols and there is a water sports centre.  However, it lacks the facilities of some of the smaller local beaches with beach side restaurants.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Night Visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A very different perspective on a visit to this lovely beach. In the evening it is very peaceful, there are few people on the  beach and it is a totally different experience e to the crowded day.There were fishermen to watch and a few others walking enjoying an evening walk.A very relaxing experience

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Portugal summer Vac
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Falesia and its surrounding beaches ,shops,restaurants, coffee shops and fantastic accommodation is the one stop shop of vacations. Always a pleasure to visit here-always want to come back

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Busy beach  - don't bother!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The pictures of this beach are nothing like the reality. It is very busy and overcrowded. Not a pleasant experience and certainly not worth the steps down to it!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: August 2018
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The fabulous beach 'Praia da Falesia runs from Olhos de Agua in the west all the way east to Vilamoura, with numerous beach accesses to choose from.But here's an insider tip; drive in the direction of the Alfamar Hotel and then east to Roxa Baixinha. The tarmac road then goes to a dirt road for another 750 meters where you will find the entrance to 'Praia dos Tomates' (Tomato Beach). Parking just off the beach will cost you 2.50€ for the day in high season, but believe me, it is worth it!The beach is just fabulous, with long stretches of white sand and a gentle slope into the turquoise waters, with the amazing back drop of low orange-hued cliffs.When the heat gets too much - and it will - there is a beach bar at the entrance to the beach called 'Quebra Côco' (broken coconut), where they serve cool beer in iced glasses and have a delicious array of snacks and salads.Life just doesn't get any better!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A nice, long and wide beach. Possibility to park the car nearby. A small bar nearby. Only cold water...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Never on a Sunday in August
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Arrived around 1pm and eventually managed to find parking.  Walked along to the wooden steps down to the beach and was greeted with the human equivalent of an ant colony.  The beach was packed like I have never seen before and as we live on the Costa Del Sol we see a lot of beaches!Stayed less than an hour.  Sunbeds all taken so no shade. It may be as beautiful as other reviewers say when it's a bit quieter but this day was the worst beach experience I have ever had.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Heaven
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is one of the best beaches we have been to . The rocks above it make it  magical and as if it is something from Jurassic Park ! Stunning views and very wild. Has clean toilets and showers . Has a couple of cafe shops / bars for light lunch . Guarded beech as well. Bring your own parasol, cold bag, sun protection and you will be in Heaven !

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Spent a great day at this beach recently. It offers great facilities; beach umbrellas, sun loungers, showers, toilets and plenty of restaurants. The highlight were the water activities. We went parasailing and hired a pedalo too. All in all a great day at the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fantastic beach - absolutely perfect place to spend the day with your family. Beach is as natural as can be - the sea water is freezing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was the most beautiful beach we visited in Algarve. We have visited several beaches in the area from Lagos up to Albufeira and this has been my top pick. The water was actually warmer and crystal clear with out any seaweed. There weresome waves but small enough to feel safe with the Kids swiming. Ideal for Kids and families. There is a small restaurant that sells pizza and sandwiches and ice cold beer! But bring your own food and water because there is not much to buy. It was so beautiful we stayed to watch the sunset.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach near restaurants
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely beach where you can pay for a lounger or bring your own accessories. Near restaurants and shops.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Praid de Falesia - great for early morning runs
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely stretch of beach running from Olhos d'agua to Vilamoura.  Early morning when the tide was out enjoyed jogging along in the relative cool.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Most beautiful Falesia Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the most beautiful beach. It is our 4th stay at the Portobay.  They have built a new wooden stair access (100+ steps)  with handrails down to beach.  We stay to the right side. There are padded lounge chairs with umbrellas available for 15 euros for the full day. It is a guarded beach.  When the tide is out you can enjoy a pretty walk across the rocks all the way to the Olhos d Agua beach/town. There are bathroom facilites and a full restaurant, O Golfino, perfect for lunch or snack, reservations taken. There is a shower also available, but is not free.  Perfect beach, the red cliffs topped with dark green pines and the whitest cleanest sand as far as you can see and the beautiful Atlantic ocean in front, more than beautiful. Be sure to enjoy the bolinhas they walk around to sell.  I even bought a beautiful beach. Bolinhas are the best.Blanket from a sand vendor, you can sit back and they pass right by.  Very enjoyable beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach in the algarve.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the finest beach we have ever visited. Very long, white sand, clear blue water, safe for children, clean.Plenty of places to nip off for a bit of food or drink. Definitely don't miss this one.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous if a little busy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wonderful stretch of sand, if you head further down the beach it is quieter. The first beach on the right is very good, the second is high end with high prices

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach, has wooden steps to access with a small cafe bar for snacks and drinks. The sand is lovely, and has beds and umbrellas to rent.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Worth the trek
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a spectacular beach which I understand is four miles long. We were staying at Clube Humbria in Olhos D’Agua which has its own beach. However that beach is ok but gets quite busy. It is a 10/15 min walk from our hotel whereas Falesia beach is 20 mins but well worth the trek. We walked the first time but with two small children we tried a taxi the second time. This was a mistake as we were dropped a mile further along the beach where the nearest road access allowed. So we walked back along the beach to our favourite spot nearer to where our walk had taken us on the first visit and where we hired loungers and there were rock pools for shrimping , crabbing and fishing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: lovely views and sunsets
reviewsWithKeywords.text: worth a look, sandy and Little Rock pools for the kids to look in too.   probably need decent shoes to walk on this beach though.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful expansive beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach seems to go on for ever. It is worth taking the time to walk to the quieter sections in the middle. The water is also clearer there. Take a picnic and parasol and set yourself up for the day. Some water sports available and parasol and lounger hire. Very little natural shade. The cliffs are stunning.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach Bums
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful beach with steps going down to the beach. The sand wasn't too hot to walk on and the sea was a bit chilly.The beach has a lifeguard and sunloungers and parasols. The parasol get taken up quick.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach but too busy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Visited late in the day. Unless you are ultra early, leave the car at the top of the track because parking on the beach is a nightmare.  Apart from that it's ok.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely relaxing beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach never over crowded. Clean and relaxing  and be accessed from Porto Bay Falesia hotel. Great day for all

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Many of the beaches in the Algarve that we’ve visited have been scenic but very packed. This beach is both scenic and has lots of room to spread out without feeling you were on top of people. There is a vendor at the top of the cliff before descending down the stairs to the beach that sells beach items (towels, beach toys, umbrellas, etc) that was helpful. Great day all around!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: good trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: perfect beach for relaxing and rest, good for long walks and chill in the sun. easy access to the sea.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sandy gem
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beach very clean and stretches for miles. Very popular when we were there. There is a car park but I'm unsure how it is accessed. There are toilets and showers and place to eat. Would suggest a few more waste bins. Water very clear but beware of the drag of the waves it can be quite strong. Also freezing!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Go to this beach from Clube Humbria not the Praia dos Olhos de Agua which is pebbly small overcrowded and has loads of seaweed.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful, large beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach. Yes it's busy with tourists but the beach is so large my girlfriend and I found a spot easily with more than ample space. Waves were extremely fun and not harsh. We parked down the hill from where you turn to go into the beach so it was a 5-10 minute walk but not too bad. Check out the restaurants down the hill for some amazing piri piri chicken and gelato ice cream. Happy travels!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Quiet , well kept . And lovely . Loungers available at a cost . Restaurant there which sells drinks and ice creams too

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cliff top view and clean beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fantastic view from the cliff top that run all the way along the beach, the road down to the beach is very steep and then you have to walk down a wooden staircase, some older visitors may find the walk difficult especially but up the hill,

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Day Visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice few hours here , very busy & touristy . Lovely beach & great views . Lots to do , lots of bars & restaurants to eat & drink .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Recommend a visit - enjoyable experience
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Recommend a visit - enjoyable experience, especially when weather is very hot. Plenty of available facilities - view excellent.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fab
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved it! Spent two days there, watersports were great fun, definitely worth a visit. Parking was awkward though and be aware there’s a lot of steps

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice safe family beach right next to the marina
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is the nearest to the marina and is busy in July and August. It has 3 good beach bars/restaurants. It is popular with young families as the sea is pretty calm and shallow.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A walk down 137 steps which seems like 20. Clean sandy beach stretching for miles. Very cold water! 🤤 Still inviting. 🏊‍♂️

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Although this beach is amazing, it could be an issue for anyone not good at walking, climbing stairs or with heights phobias. There are steps down to the beach but there is a lot of them.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beach is Clean and locals friendly. The cafe at the top supply hot and cold food and a lovely shaded area to eat .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Recommended a visit . A clean beach with plenty of sunbeds.  There is a bar / restaurant so you can get a drink and of course there are toilets.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The beach of all beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wow this beach must be 5 or 6 miles long of beautiful sand in a clear pale green sea. Lots of entertainment in the form of watersports in various places up and down the beach along with places to eat, along with sunloungers and shade should you wish to rent them. Waves are good too, its one of those places if your near you have to go and visit

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Looking to soak up some sun and have FUN.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We loved the area, the beach the atmosphere,too bad the water was too cold for swimming, other than that we enjoyed our visit.You can get an area with two beach chairs and umbrella for €18 for a whole day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Swimming
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach however overpriced restaurants that are not worth it. Plus the energy is not good down there ! There are plenty better beaches that you should see ;)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Red sand but nothing special
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you are close to the beach you should give it a try. But if you are coming form another part of the town just to see it don't bother. You will find a red sand beach, but  noting special in my opinion.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There’s honestly not a lot I can say about it, you really have to be there to experience it. Lying on it is relaxing, and the view of the ocean is breath-taking.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach views.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing place for clifftop walks. We aren't the types to lie on the beach these days but there were plenty who did and the area is very clean and well kept.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: very clean beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: nice sunchairs and relaxing. good bar and restaurant - water a bit cold but nice to walk on this beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Perfect
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A very long beach 6 miles I think I was told clean fresh sands sun all day sun cream and brolly`s a must vast amounts of cliff faces all with fab colours and flowers, a few beach bars serving the normal if here with young children please ensure they are covered up even on a cloudy day.  you can go down, at night to watch the sun sets you will not be disappointed. You can if you want walk 1 way to Albufeira just watch the tides, the other way to Vilamoura or just pop round the corner to Olhos D Auga olld fishing village another beach bars and shops not to be missed. On the beach you can hire beds and brolly`s at a price take your own.Save some drink for the climb back up.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: beautiful beach well worth a visit especially at nightime gorgeous sunsets as well.ideal for walks brilliant

reviewsWithKeywords.title: First visit not the last
reviewsWithKeywords.text: 1st visit to this hotel and not the last. The hotel is spotless, rooms and beds are large, and atmosphere is relaxing and happy. The manager Carlos know how to get the best out of his staff. Every member from the great waiters and bar staff and cleaners were so very helpful, accommodating  and friendly. Everybody had a smile on their face including the guests. The entertainment team,Harry,Chloe,Dani , Dom and the house band Panache were wonderful. But a special mention must go to Harry , who's sense of humour and caring attitude to every guest made our holiday even more special. The guy needs a commendation from TUI.We'll be back next year God willing. Rob and Liza

reviewsWithKeywords.title: 50th Birthday
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach not to busy. Couple of cafesQuite a few steps down to it so not for anyone with walking difficulties.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful long sandy cliff lined quiet beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is our favourite past time walking around Vilamoura marina over the small pedestrian bridge & then along the beautiful cliff lined beach as far as we can & then stop & have a beer at one of the cafe/bats along the route then walk home. There are quality facilities along the beach more spread out the further from Vilamoura you venture, the cliff formations are worth the wander alone, the perfect day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Quiet
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very nice beach, quiet and lots of space to find your own spot. Safe for kids although in June the weather was a bit windy and not so hot and the water was just 18 degrees but felt v cold.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love this place!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The reception staff were very friendly & helpful. The apartment, 1232, was spacious, comfortable & clean. All outside areas were immaculate. We had bed & breakfast, the food was great. We had one dinner there, it was reasonably priced. We ate out every in the village every night, plenty of choice. Lovely walk down to the beach from the resort. Hired chair beds & brolly, very comfortable, 15euros a day. Beach cafe was also very good. We hope to return in early October!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Glorious long beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Miles & miles of soft sand with only the Atlantic Ocean on the horizon. Fantastic to walk along at low tide. Backed by cliffs, with various access points up wooden steps for well trodden cliff walks with stunning views. Sunbeds for hire at intermittent points along the way, with mile after mile of empty beach in between. There is a regular bus service from Albufeira, takes about 25 minutes, a worthwhile day out, which picks up at Oura Intermarche,  St Eulalia, & Olhus d'Agua.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Miles and miles of golden sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Miles and miles of golden sand describes this beach pretty well. Although busy there was plenty of space so it never felt crowded. The beach is clean and safe with toilets near by. I can strongly recommend hitting one of the restaurants close byto have a Somersby Apple cider to cool off.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just a fabulous beach. Clean accessible and beautiful. Plenty of space. Beach bars are great. Will come back

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely sandy beach where, if you walk a little you can be away from the crowds or you can stay near the entrances and beach restaurants and still not be too crowded. The sea is not as cold as the English Channel but then only the Artic is colder than the English seas! There are life guards at certain points but the sea can be choppy and does shelve quickly so it is important to keep a close eye on children. The cliffs are fascinating in their colours and formations. And finally if you fancy a decent beach walk then there are 7 km of continuous sand to enjoy starting from the marina at Vilamora.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A sandy cove in centre of Albufeira
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Cove surrounded by cliffs, some nice rock pools for children and stronger swimmers can swim out to marked bouys.  Beach with sunbeds for hire and a restaurant/bar/toilets.  Walk cliffs to reach Old Town in 15-20 mins.   Limited parking right down at the beach if follow the beach signs from the main road (near MacDonalds junction)  and arrive before midday.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: best beach to visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: i would definitly recommend going to Falesia beach as its beautiful and breathtaking:)there might be a struggle with parking a car in a busy peak time as its limited.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach that is not crowded at all. Plenty of room for everyone. Not suitable for wheelchair since there are many steps and stairs down to the beach from road and parking.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Whilst it is a long way down a lot of steps the time and effort spent is well worth the effort.  Turn left at the bottom and you can walk for 5 miles to Villamora. The beach is clean and comfortable sand to walk on with fantastic scenery with cliffs of a variety of shades.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful in every aspect
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The views are outstanding. It's not very crowded and loungers are available for about €17-19 for two with an umbrella

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning beach with a couple of nice places to eat sun beds with umbrellas to hire ( not sure of cost as we did not use them )

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Magical
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I go there every year it's a clean well kept beach i can spend all day here  and the light and the views are just breath taking

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Day out
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We walked 30 minutes to get to beach and the views were amazing there is a bar at the top of the steps so you can get cold drinks and food

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the most beautiful beaches in Algarve
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very nice and beautiful beach, not overcrowded  (at least in the middle of June). There is a very nice view from above:)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach provides for all the famiky ..fun optiins for sport , swimming and more . Long walks for romantics and fab restaurants to chill under the setting sun. Clean facilities with showers also available

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great place for lots of photos. The beach is beautiful. There are lovely local restaurants nearby like Neptuno and Frango Real. There prices are cheap for a snack, lunch or dinner. Fabulous walks along the beach into Vilamoura or Olhos de agua. If you have kids or mobility issues there is parking on the main road leading down to the beach but it can get very busy during summer. There is quite a few steps leading down to the beach but well worth it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Walking
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely beautiful beach to walk. Goes on and on. Even the odd place to stop for s beer or coffee. Great for photography

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely walk to nearest town velermoura. Restaurants.life guards toilets . Think wheel chair may struggle as it's Sandy beach .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Falésia Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice rocks with intensive colours mixing the red, white and some yellow just beside the blue ocean  - it is wonderful. I took a walking tour from the bus station at Pine Cliffs stop beside nice hotels and pines. At the end of the walking tour I found this really nice Beach. Lovely sandy beach with red rocks, parasols, plants. Unforgettable adventure

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is quite simply one of the most beautiful beaches in the area.If you like long sandy beaches, with clear safe water to swim in then look no further.You can walk as far as Vilamoura marina if you have the energy, or just a stroll along to one of the beach bars dotted along the long beach.Parking can get busy, so you can drive to further points along the beach to find other parking. If you are prepared to walk a bit, you will find your own space on the beach.Fantastic cliff formations and erosin to look at.A great walk a long the beach and back along the top of the cliff if you like a circular walk!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning beach. Beautiful setting. Long steps down to get on the beach, but definitely worth it. Fantastic backdrop of cliffs.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: stunning scenery!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: the scenery is awesome   and almost white sand !! we walked from villamoura to  falesia  and  its stunning

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Falesia beach is elected one of the most beautiful beach in the world; it deserves this title 100%:A mixture of the national parks in the USA; Brice Canon, Zion , Canon de Chelly, etc

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Popular, yet quiet
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We've been there on 2 June. Sea is freezing cold during that time of the year. Well, if you're not a nordic family. :) Family friendly beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very clean and beautiful beach , beautiful views. Everyone has to visit. Few restaurans in the beach. Definately recomending.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very good
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We found the beach was kept very clean with good facilities , we would definitely make a return trip to this area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just gorgeous!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is spotless, unspoilt with access to 2 restaurants/bars which have easy accessible toliets and showers outside. No need to worry about cutting through the restaurant to go to the toliet. For 3 sun loungers it cost us 13 euro per day, very reasonably priced.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely beach with golden sands, toilets and a bar so got your comfort stops, this is a beach that doesn't get crowded thankfully, must also say Galway entertainer you are very wrong about the bullfighting the Bull is not killed, nor is it tortured I've not seen any of the Bulls bleed the whole event is carefully choreographed all the animals are very well cared for

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: An absolute must see if you're in this area. It's an incredible place to walk and relax. The cliffs really are breathtaking, many pictures don't do them justice. The most beautifl and peaceful place I think I've been.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great little beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Was lovely and quiet when we went.. so so peaceful. There is also a bar and toilets at tge beach entrance for comfort stops.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The water quality is excellent. Always sunny. Very clean beach and extremely safe. Perfect for families. Any person's dream holiday - I highly recommend this beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Overpriced deck chairs but nice beaxh
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The red cliffs are stunning and the beach is lovely, however the sand is quite coarse compared to Sao Rafael beach and the deckchairs were overpriced!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Long, clean beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Typical Algarve beach, in that it's backed with cliffs making for a walk down but that is what gives it the scenic appeal.Seems OK for swimming and good for just pottering, walking or doing nothing. Couple of places for refreshments.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Falesia Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach was excellent was very clean and extended for miles we were able to walk along tthe beach to the next town of Vilamoura . First class. Water cold in May though.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Calm and beautiful place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach was by to the hotel and was so beautiful and calm. This place offer a nice infra structure and you can rent a chair and umbrella for all or half day... Also you can find a restaurant or you can enjoy a massage at the beach. The only thing is that in May the sea is cold, sometimes impossible to get some sun refreshing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great clean beach - not croweded beginnig of may
reviewsWithKeywords.text: this beach is extremely clean and we travled here in the first week of May and was not crowded at all -- only down side is there are solicitors begging you to buy sunglasses, blankets and other trinkets, mostly from Africa

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love this beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A long, sandy beach which we always enjoy during our visits to the Algarve.  There are places to have  can obviously sunbathe to your hearts content or if like us you just like to stroll along the sand the this is the place to do it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Mikes of clean sand and blue waters
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We traveled by bus from Faro.Very regular service.Hiwever check the timetable as there is a break in the middle of the day.These buses get crowded as they collect from the airport but if you get in / off at the terminal end/beginning...Far or the beach....you’ll be fine.We couldn’t see access to public toilets although there are plenty of cafes and restaurants.Very clean beaches..not filled with load music.Loved it

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a stunning beach on which you can walk for miles.I would recommend a visit.It is beside Villamoura and a great escape for a more laid back day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach - fantastic scwnery
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved this beach, amazing scenery & lovely places to eat or get a drink. It must get very busy here on high season

reviewsWithKeywords.title: gorgeous beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nearest beach to our hotel. Just over 100 steps down and back up, but shaded areas with benches to have a rest if you need it. Car parking available (quite small) down there, but an awkward bit of road (?) to negotiate with craters and potholes. Glad I didn't have to drive.Plenty of sand, nice for dipping the toes in the sea. A few places for an eat and drink, toilets. Beautiful orange colour of the cliffs against the pure blue sky.All in a lovely spot. Plenty of room for everyone. Recliners and parasols to hire in various places.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Travelled with small toddler & 4 adultsBeach amazing, lovely sand, heat trapWe took some beers to beach as no bars localVery cleanLifeguards on part of beach to Adriana beach club hotel

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Golden Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A wonderful beach which was located just next to our hotel. My girlfriend and I walked the length of the beach to Vilamoura, which is around 7km, and enjoyed every bit of it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The place behind the pines
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Marvelous beach. One hundred wooden steps guided us from the hotel to the beach, passing through a pine forrest. Fine sand, spectacular yellow-red-green cliffs....and the continous sound of the ocean. Clean and not overcrowded.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A beautiful blue flag beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was in front of our hotel down exactly 128 steps - quite steep going back up but with seats strategically placed to rest.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most beautiful beaches I have ever seen. So picturesque.We stayed at the Adriana Beach Club and had to swipe in and out of the hotel to access the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the highlights of our trips, beach was spotless and not overly busy. Great atmoshphere and my son loved it

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful and not busy (yet)
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Definitely a great beach to visit when you're in the Algarve. The water is only a bit cold in May! The only thing we missed was a little bar or restaurant at the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach but not easily accessible
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning beach, spotlessly clean and plenty of loungers etc. Steep hill to climb down followed buy lots of wooden steps - even worse coming back up!!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: big stretch of beach in southern portugal
reviewsWithKeywords.text: the sand is shell to Orange colored.the waters are blue green from the Atlantic. clean overall.lots of people on the beach. if you're staying at the hotels like epic sana, they have direct access to the beachfront.i believe it's a much longer walk from public.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice and sandy but lots of rocks.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Because of the spectacular cliffs the beach has lots of rocks. You can only go so far and have to watch where you are walking in some places. You also have to know the tide times because if you attempt to cross the large rocks in places you can get cut off.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: stunning beach & views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is one of the most beautiful in the Algarve. Follow signs to the beach.At the end of the road, it makes a left turn and down a hill, (or you drive over the cliff into the ocean).When you reach the point of the left turn, It is possible to turn right and park there at the top of the hill, under the trees. At the bottom of the hill are the access stairs to the beach. There are not a lot of stairs, and there are benches to rest at every 1/3 of the way. There is a snack & drink shop at the top of the stairs. They sell beer, tea, coffee, ice cream, and snacks. All of the seating is outdoor. Take care around the cliffs. There have been a lot of winter storms and a lot of erosion. Do not get close to the edge of cliffs and keep hold of small children. When you are on the beach, take care and don't set up camp too close to the cliffs. Rocks and earth are eroding quickly after the storms. For everyone's safety, stay off the cliffs where danger exists.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's the second time we visited the beach and won't be the last! Amazing views, once you there you might want to wait for the sunset, it will worth it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We came on an over cast day and a sunny day and enjoyed both. lots to explore and find. Good for shells and birdwatching

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were staying at the nearby Epic SANA hotel which has direct access to this lovely sandy beach. The sand was clean and the sea not too chilly. Sun beds and parasols are available to hire but they weren’t available when we were there due to it not being the main season. There is a reasonably priced snack bar, just up from the main stairs selling a variety of drinks, snacks and ice creams.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So lovely to walk along paddling in the sea and plenty of bars along the beach for a refreshing drink

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Home sweet home
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I've lived in the Algarve all my life so I'm pretty familiar with the majority of beaches, and this one is definetly one of my favourites. These cliffs are just beautiful and different. If you've been to the algarve before you know that majority of cliffs are alike, they look like they're made of sand and not many of them look like this. The beach is clean, the water is clear, and it's perfect for a sunrise and a sunset walk, as the views and its colours are a feast to the eyes. Definetly recommend.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We walked along the beach, stopped for a drink in the beach cafe and it was delightful. It is a beautiful beach and lovely to walk over the rocks.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is spectacular, surrounded by stunning views and rustic rock. It’s a great place for walks and just to sit, relax & soak up the views. A great spot for every one

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pretty
reviewsWithKeywords.text: pretty beach and a nice treat to stop by to see. We were there a day after a rainstorm and it was interesting to see the pools of colors in the sand that washed down from the cliffs.  Keep in mind that when you step to the edges of the overlooks, the cliffs are only sand. I was surprised that there werent more warnings.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Going there for surf
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I like the place where is not crowed by season tourist, wonderful cost for biking and nice calm peak for surfing :)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Atlantic escape
reviewsWithKeywords.text: AMAZING natural beach, great waves, walks, views, sea air. So good for the soul and well being. We love this beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely rich sand and gentle waves on the day we were there plus the spectacular cliffs all added up to a good visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We're used to Caribbean beaches, which are quite different from these. The cliffs are spectacular. It was too early in the season to fully enjoy the beach and the sea. The venues were still closed. We really enjoyed the walk on the beach and the views. Took some very nice pics.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of my favourite places on Earth
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beauty the tranquillity the colours the temperature the noises and the smells what a beautiful place to visit.  Great for walking lovely and clean great for families having fun lovely clear warm waters for children to swim safely and the scenery.  Did I mention I liked it ?

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Endless beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went here on a rather overcast day. Endless beach with dramatic cliff backdrop. You could walk for hours here. Very beautiful and well worth a visit. You could spend a whole day here in good weather. Natural setting and not commercialised at all.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is clean and had plenty of cafes along the way for refreshments and restrooms. We walked across the beach to Valimore. Recommend a visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a nice beach when you want a place without wind.  The beach is very long so ideal for a beach walk.  I went in april so it was not to crowded.  I don't know if it's nice in summer.  I doubt that because it's in a very touristic area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful long beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: These beaches are well worth a visit.  They are very long and whether you want a long walk or a quiet sit, play or swim, they are beautiful.  Life guards also have a presents as well as visit by local police in their jeeps.  There are regular drinking a eating spots along the beach.The beach, however, has steep cliffs and is therefore only accessible at certain points along the cliffs.  We accessed through Pine Cliffs, down a lift and then down some easily accessible step, graduated, 3/4 step then a 2 metre flat, then repeated.  Other places to access where with steps and the a hill up.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So this beach is amazing also it was near to where we stayed, I would not advise any one to visit if they are not very mobile as there are many steps down to the beach. But once there it's so beautiful, with fine powdery sand which stays cool under a hot sun, it must be miles long and looks spectacular because it's lined with these Sandy coloured cliffs the whole time. Only thing is if you leave something in the car or want something in the shop it's a trek back up. But all the same well worth visiting.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Holiday
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Pleasant beach area with cafes,bars and restaurants to suit all tastes and budgets.Toilet block which we didn't need to use.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: " Praia da Falesia "
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Falesia Beach is part of a continuous stretch of sand which is approximately 7 km in length. It has a dramatic backdrop of high cliffs which are rich in colours ranging from reds to cream. The erosion of the cliffs provides deep grooves and gullies and in some areas the sand has formed what looks like giant termite mounds. There is access along the top of the cliffs with meandering path ways through pine groves and stunning vistas towards the sea. Please be advised that although there are some warning signs pertaining to the dangers of the cliffs, there are no barriers or fences, so families need to be vigilant regarding the safety of their loved ones.  I visited this beach in March 2018 and some days I could walk for miles without seeing another person. I would imagine that this would all change during the main holiday season as this beach is very popular with tourists and the local population. My advice is to visit this beach out of season to appreciate its beauty, tranquillity and cleanliness. The wild life on this part of the coast especially birds is very good. I saw many Waders, Red Legged Partridge, Hoopoe & Azure Winged Magpie. Also, there were the first signs of summer approaching with Swallows and Martins along with Sardinian Warblers and Black Redstarts arriving daily. Falesia Beach in my humble opinion is very impressive. However, it is not the easiest beach to access especially from the Olhos de Agua end. There are wooden stairways to negotiate which have hundreds of steps to and from the beach so this could prove problematic for some people.  Also, it is prudent to check the tide times as the sea can come in very quickly in some areas and you will find your beach walk cut off by the incoming tide.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful and unspoilt
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A beautiful and unspoilt beach. Must be Three miles long. It sits at the bottom of cliffs so access for disabled is an issue. Lovely walks with unbelievable views along the cliff paths above the beach. You can hire beds and wind breaks and the beach does have some beach bars but not a lot. Unspoilt is the watchword and very beautiful and dramatic

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Needs a clean
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beach needs addressing a few safety issuesThe walk ways are unsafeAnd a good tidy would help lots of rubbish and unsafe rock which isn't protected by any say netting, there is a safety signBut they still allow people on the beachIt's an accident waiting to happen.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is well worth the visit. It was a beautiful walk along the sand with the amazing cliffs as a backdrop. There were a lot of people walking and enjoying the peace and quiet. We came back via the road and it was only then we realised how far we had walked.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Decent beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Decent beach with plenty of food places very very near . Sunbeds to hire and rocks to explore .watersports available

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Simply stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is one of the loveliest child friendly beaches I have visited in the Algarve.  With the ability to go out pretty far and still be shallow, it was excellent for my adventurous child.  The cliffs as a backdrop and stunning and they walk back either up the road or back toward olhos dagua beach round the rocks is very pleasant.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful and expansive beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stunning beach, with soft sand, goes on for miles. Deckchairs were 6 euros when we went. Only slight negatives were the long set of steps to get down to shoreline which may cause an issue for the elderly or those with a pram.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice stretch of beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We accessed this beach from the top of the hill and there is a new staircase (129 steps to be precise!) built to gain access to the beach. Once on the beach there is a nice stretch of clean sand but there wasn't any sunbeds???This beach was not busy at all so you could pick wherever you wanted to set up camp 😄 There are a couple of restaurants scattered about which offer really nice food and drink.Worth a visit if in the area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We walked along the beach from Vilamoura not realising that we had walked all the way to this lovely beach.  We returned in the car and walked the rest of the way along the other way as the whole beach from Vilamoura is over 7 km long.  Really great cliffs back the beach all the way along and safe paths too, otherwise I would not normally recommend walking on the cliffs in the Algarve as they can be dangerous.  Lovely beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Superb beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Miles of golden sand. Walk to Villamoura in two hours. Photo opportunities by amazing cliffs all the way.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: As beautiful as 30 years ago
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I visited here almost 30 years ago with my girlfriend who is now my wife. This year we have our son with his girlfriend with us and the beach was as beatiful as before.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach with family
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Staying at the Pine Cliffs resort and really enjoyed the beach here. Very accessible for the kids which are ages 10, 8, and 4. Low waves and good sandcastle making.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach walked to vilamora and back every day .Exceptionally clean and the scenery is stunning

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: In our last day in the Algarve, before our flight at 7 PM, we got the car and drove around many different places. We started quite early, at 7 AM to get the low tide, that allows people to see the water springs in Olho D'água. It is interesting to see non-salt water coming out from the sand. The springs are on the right hand side of the beach, but do not expect massive springs, they are small ones and you need to pay attention to the ground, they can only be seen during the low tide. There are some pools in which you can sit and relax, but as it was early in the morning, it was still cold for us to do that. We walked along the beach and through the "Falesias". Albufeira is a beautiful place and there is a lot to be explored. You can spend a day at Olho D'água or Falesia beach, as there are  restaurants along the coast, but you can also organize a day trip to see some beaches. Try a walk and enjoy the views from the top of the cliffs. In April it was cold in the morning, but the temperature rose by midday. We decided to wear trainners as we were doing some walks on the top of the cliffs, but we had flip flops and beach wear in the backpack, so we could also enjoy the beaches. You only need a couple of hours in each beach and it took us only 20 minute to drive between them. As I am from Rio and I had traveled to many places with astonishing coast in Brazil, a beach needs to be outstanding to blow me up, do not get me wrong, the ones in the Algarve are beautiful, but I think the walks above the cliffs and exploring the country side is a lot more worth it. If you enjoy spending a day by the sea, though, go for it, the infrastructure to make you comfortable is there!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We enjoyed a wonderful stroll here yesterday . Gorgeous long sandy beach  that stretches from Olhas D”Água  towards Vilamoura.  It was a pleasure to enjoy the views . There are a few cafes either end of the beach if you wished to stop off en route . Well worth a visit !

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful and clean sand beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very clean and clear beach. Has a long coastal line which is nice for a walk.As we visited in first week of April water was a bit cold for a swim.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Albufeira beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of many stunning beaches on the Algarve we visited during our 3 week holiday.Recommended to all visitors. .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Excellent beach. Very clean. I really enjoyed staying on this beach.  Lots of local restaurants and a wide variety of shops all within easy reach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic beach and views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach was amazing, the view from the hotel looking done was fab (pic 1) the others were taken from the beach looking out to sea and up at the cliffs.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Found this by accident after having a coffee in Neptune’s Bar. Bit of a steep walk but well worth the view

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach, very clean , lots of stairs but lift back up. You can walk from vilamoura all the way along.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Clean, calm & relaxing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Clean and close to large car park. Busy in the summer but were the only ones there today, probably due to the weather! Can't believe someone reviewed this beach as 'gritty'!!!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular red and white cliffs
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A huge beach to the east of albufeira. Beautiful colours in the cliff. Wide sandy beach. Good wooden staircase down to the beach. Not a lot of parking considering the size of the beach. The small cafe at  the stairs has decent washrooms.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Boys trip
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Was unable to sample the beach as the weather was pretty horrible. Beach looked very clean but sandy looked imported and quite gritty.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Alfarmar
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stayed at the Alfarmar, walked to villa ours, beautiful beaches, clean and nice. Not a lot of restaurants but probably because it’s still out of season. Enjoyed the views though

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Took my breath away
